source_basis.staged_description: NPR’s February 24, 2026 investigation examined whether records listed in files related to Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell were present in the Justice Department’s public database. That review led NPR to report that dozens of pages appeared to be catalogued by the department but unavailable to the public. In one instance involving a woman who accused Donald Trump, NPR identified 53 pages of interview documents and notes that appeared to be missing. Records showed that the FBI interviewed the woman four times; the only interview then available publicly was the first, and it did not mention Trump. NPR emphasized that the allegation was unverified, and its reporting does not establish that Trump committed wrongdoing. DOJ declined to answer specific questions on the record, then said unpublished material was privileged, duplicative or connected to an ongoing investigation. NPR documented a discrepancy in what was publicly available, not proof of the allegation or a contradiction in Trump’s defense.
